newsitem.title: USA: New sex charges against top U.S. enlisted soldier.
newsitem.headline: New sex charges against top U.S. enlisted soldier.

text.p: A sixth military woman has accused Sergeant Major of the Army Gene McKinney of sexual misconduct, prompting two new charges against the top U.S. enlisted soldier, the Army said on Friday.

The new charges -- maltreatment of a subordinate and assault -- brought to 22 the number of charges being investigated by a military preliminary hearing to decide whether McKinney should face a court-martial.
If the court-martial occurred and McKinney were convicted of all charges, the maximum possible penalty would be 57.5 years in prison.

The latest accusations were made by a woman sergeant first class at a U.S. Army recruiting station in the southeastern United States, the Army said in a statement. A spokesman for the Military District of Washington declined to give further details.

McKinney, a 29-year veteran, has denied all charges and applied for retirement with full benefits. As the first African-American to hold his prominent post, he alleged racial bias in the Army's investigation.
The first five women to accuse McKinney were white. Information about the race of the latest accuser was not released.
The preliminary hearing, taking place at Fort McNair in Washington, was in recess until Aug. 11.
